title: Chlorella Virus Plaque Assay
author: Dr. Steven Wilhelm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.hgqb3vw

steps.title: Prepare soft agar overlay
steps.instruction: Melt MBBM soft agar, dispense into 3.0 mL aliquots, and keep at 45 °C–50 °C in a water bath until use.

steps.title: Concentrate Chlorella cells
steps.instruction: Spin Chlorella at 5,000 rpm for 5 min at 4 °C, concentrate to 4.0 × 10⁸ cells/mL, and resuspend in fresh MBBM so that 0.3 mL is available per plate.

steps.title: Make virus serial dilutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the virus in 50 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 7.8, using 1 : 10 serial dilutions; note that fresh lysate is ~10⁶–10⁷ PFU/mL and dilute to obtain 20–200 PFU per plate.

steps.title: Combine agar, virus, and cells
steps.instruction: To each 3.0 mL soft agar aliquot, add 0.1 mL virus and 0.3 mL concentrated Chlorella, mix by rolling between palms, pour onto an MBBM plate, tilt gently to spread evenly, and allow the agar to solidify.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.1 mL virus and 0.3 mL Chlorella to 3.0 mL agar
Pour onto MBBM plate and tilt gently to cover surface

steps.title: Incubate and count plaques
steps.instruction: Incubate plates at 25 °C under continuous light for 3–4 days (or until plaques appear), then use a Sharpie to mark and count visible plaques.
